Q-Analysis

Source: R/simplicial.R
q_analysis.Rd

q_analysis() describes how the maximal simplices of a simplicial complex (those not contained in a larger one) hang together, after Atkin (1974). Two maximal simplices are q-near when they share a face of dimension at least q (q + 1 shared nodes), and q-connected when a chain of q-near simplices joins them. The result has two parts:

  • Q-vector: \(Q_q\), the number of q-connected components among the maximal simplices of dimension at least q, for each q from the largest simplex dimension down to 0. Simplices of lower dimension do not exist at level q and are not counted.

  • Structure vector: here the dimension of the largest simplex each node belongs to. (Atkin uses "structure vector" for the Q-vector itself; the name is kept for compatibility.)

A Q-vector of 1 at every level means the maximal simplices stay in one piece however many shared nodes are required. Requiring more shared nodes splits the complex more, but fewer simplices take part at higher q, so the count can rise or fall with q; print() reports the lowest level at which there is more than one. Like the complex itself, the vectors depend on the threshold or pathways build_simplicial() was given.

Usage

q_analysis(sc)

# S3 method for class 'q_analysis'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'q_analysis'
plot(x, combined = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

sc

A simplicial_complex from build_simplicial().

x

For the print() and plot() methods: a q_analysis object.

...

For the print() and plot() methods: ignored.

combined

For the plot() method: TRUE (default) draws the Q-vector and the structure vector side by side, which needs gridExtra; FALSE returns them as a named list of ggplots (q_vector, structure_vector).

Value

A q_analysis object. print() shows the components at each level, the level at which the complex first splits and the structure vector; plot() draws the two vectors. The object's fields:

q_vector

Named integer vector, one entry per level from the highest down (q_2, q_1, q_0 for a complex of dimension 2): the number of q-connected components at that level.

max_q

The largest simplex dimension, the highest level.

structure_vector

Named integer vector, one entry per node: the dimension of the largest simplex containing it.

The print() method returns its input invisibly. plot() returns the drawn grid grob invisibly with combined = TRUE, and the named list of two ggplots invisibly with combined = FALSE.

References

Atkin, R. H. (1974). Mathematical Structure in Human Affairs.

Examples

mat <- matrix(c(0,.6,.5,.6,0,.4,.5,.4,0), 3, 3)
colnames(mat) <- rownames(mat) <- c("A","B","C")
sc <- build_simplicial(mat, threshold = 0.3)
q_analysis(sc)
#> Q-Analysis (max q = 2)
#>   Components: q2:1 q1:1 q0:1
#>   Fully connected at all q levels
#>   Structure: A:2 B:2 C:2
